goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
goldens.reasoning: C2 directly describes negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator; C3 describes the same negative-offset crash in general terms. C1 is about BasePaginator, a different location.

goldens.comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
goldens.reasoning: C4 and C5 discuss whether has_global_access is the right authorization check, not the crash when organization_context.member is None.

candidates: User-controlled negative cursor offsets are passed directly to Django queryset slicing in BasePaginator.get_result() at line 182, where offset is not clamped to >= 0 when cursor.is_prev is True, causing AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported

User-controlled negative cursor offsets are passed directly to Django queryset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator at lines 877-882, where negative cursor.offset is passed through directly when enable_advanced_features is True
Negative offset vulnerability allows any authenticated user to craft a cursor with negative offset to trigger unhandled 500 errors across every paginated API endpoint - a denial-of-service vector

Authorization check mismatch: has_global_access is an org-member-level permission, not an admin privilege, contradicting the comment about authorized administrators - any org member with team-level global access can trigger OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True
The authorization check using has_global_access widens the attack surface for the negative-offset vulnerability beyond superusers to regular org members
